title: Stochastic Reachability
tagline: Compare Monte Carlo, dynamic programming, absorbing-Markov solving, and importance sampling for estimating reachability probabilities under different runtimes.

curves.label: Monte Carlo Rollouts
curves.code: for (trial=0; trial<T; trial++){ s=source; for (step=0; step<maxSteps; step++){ if (absorbing[s]) break; s = nextState(sampleFromTransition(s)); } estimate += reached?1:0; } // runtime ~ T * path length
curves.name: Monte Carlo Rollouts

curves.label: Dynamic Programming (Topological-by-SCC)
curves.code: SCCs = stronglyConnectedComponents(graph); condense = buildDAG(SCCs); p = initProb(); for (comp in reverseTopological(condense)){ for (v in comp) p[v]=solveWithinSCCUsingLocalEquations(p, comp); } // runtime ~ O(n + m)
curves.name: Dynamic Programming (Topological-by-SCC)

curves.label: Absorbing Markov Linear Solve
curves.code:
Q = transientSubmatrix(transition); b = reachTargetVector(); // solve (I - Q) x = b
x = gaussianEliminationOrIterative(Q, b); return x[source]; // dense solve ~ O(n^3)
curves.name: Absorbing Markov Linear Solve

curves.label: Importance Sampling with Adaptive Tilt
curves.code: for (trial=0; trial<T; trial++){ s=source; w=1; for(step=0; step<maxSteps; step++){ a = sampleFromTiltedPolicy(s); w *= importanceRatio(s,a); s = transition(s,a); if(absorbing[s]) break; } sum += w * reached?1:0; } // variance reduction reduces effective T
curves.name: Importance Sampling with Adaptive Tilt
